ground_truth_note: The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after 24 hours is inaccurate. According to the USDA and food safety experts, cooked rice is safe to eat for 3 to 4 days if it is refrigerated promptly and stored properly. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
note_text: Cooked rice doesn't need to be thrown out after 24 hours. When refrigerated properly in an airtight container, it stays safe for 3-6 days. The actual rule is to refrigerate it within 2 hours of cooking to prevent bacterial growth. https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad
search_results:
**No, cooked rice does not need to be thrown out after 24 hours.** When stored properly in an airtight container in the refrigerator, it remains safe for **3–6 days**, according to food safety guidelines from reliable sources.

- Riceland Foods states cooked rice can be stored in the fridge for **up to 4–6 days** and must be refrigerated within **2 hours** of cooking to prevent bacteria like Bacillus cereus[1](https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods).
- Reencle indicates **3–5 days** in the fridge at 40°F (4°C) or below in an airtight container[2](https://reencle.co/blogs/news/blogs-news-blog-safe-rice-storage-and-spoilage-guide).
- Healthline reports **3–4 days** (up to a week per some sources) in the refrigerator, with freezing extending it to 8 months; it emphasizes refrigerating promptly after cooking[3](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad).

The 24-hour claim is **incorrect**; the key risk is leaving rice at room temperature beyond 2 hours, not fridge storage time[1](https://www.riceland.com/the-riceland-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-storing-and-reheating-rice-tips-tricks-from-riceland-foods)[3](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad). Always check for off smells, mold, or texture changes before eating.
